BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook, checked against the Seller's Update draft and Disclosure Letter

---

## 1. Threshold point: reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's note says that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the review should cover only **[OPEN]** items. It also says the parties "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **We should reject this in writing.**

- **Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN].** Accepting the note would mean reviewing nothing.
- **The labels are the Seller's own.** Nothing in our playbook or on our record shows that Wattlebridge has agreed to any of these positions. Most [STANDARD] items depart directly from our playbook.
- **The note asserts agreement that does not exist.** If left unchallenged, the Seller could later argue that we acquiesced through course of dealing.

I have reviewed every clause on its merits. Our mark-up cover note should say: *"Wattlebridge has not agreed any clause in this draft. The Seller's [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation and the 'Reviewer Efficiency Note' are rejected and of no effect."*

---

## 2. Clause-by-clause departures from the playbook

### A. Limitation package

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Departure / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** | The Seller has opened at our conditional fallback. We have **no written authority from Amelia Frost** to use 20%, so we must not concede or signal it. Mark up to 25% / AUD 6.0m. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Revert to AUD 5,000. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar (tipping)** | 5x our level, and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Together with the de minimis, this would screen out a large share of realistic claims. Revert to AUD 50,000 tipping. |
| **Claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. Revert to 24 months. |
| **"Applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Blanket extension of limitations | Categories kept separate; no hidden override | This would quietly impose general-regime limits on Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants and payment obligations. Delete it and replace it with express carve-outs. |

### B. Fundamental / Title warranties
The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." **We should reject this outright.** Our position is a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. A 20% cap on title would leave us exposed for up to 80% of the price if the Seller does not in fact own what it is selling.

### C. Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
Applying limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of **any nature**" would on its face cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. **This is non-negotiable.** Insert an express carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on the deal team can waive this, so it should not be traded.

### D. Disclosure (Disclosure Letter cl 1.1–1.2)
- **Clause 1.1** deems the entire data room disclosed as at 22 September 2026. **Clause 1.2** adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and all "publicly searchable corporate records." Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure.
- The words "without limiting any specific disclosure below" make it worse. The general disclosure operates in addition to the specific disclosures, so specific disclosure ends up doing no work.
- **Timing:** the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, six weeks ago. The letter needs updating to a current date, with a bring-down mechanism to Completion. Any updated disclosure must not cure warranty breaches.
- **Clause 1.4 (non-admission)** is broadly acceptable as drafted. However, we should make sure it does not undercut the Seller's warranties or indemnities, for example by implying the Seller has not warranted the accuracy of disclosed facts.

**Pushback:** delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosures (or limit them to specifically identified documents, fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of the matter). Disclosure must not qualify Title, Capacity, Tax, or specific indemnities.

### E. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
"No claim... of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including any matter **discoverable**" from the data room or public records is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion widened by constructive knowledge. It would effectively penalise us for doing due diligence. **Delete it.** If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should apply only to the **Seller's** knowledge, limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### F. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): highest commercial risk
- Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m revenue, roughly 30% of FY26** (DD-002, clause 11.2 change-control; conditions in 11.3).
- The Seller offers **reasonable endeavours** and treats the condition as satisfied **on delivery** of written consent. Both are contrary to our playbook.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms that **no final consent and no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** exists. Calling this "addressed" is inaccurate.

**Pushback:** make it a condition precedent requiring an **effective** consent from Bluefen together with **evidence that every clause 11.3 condition has been satisfied** before Completion. The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer, with a long-stop date and a termination right. Reasonable endeavours alone is not acceptable for a customer of this materiality.

### G. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- About **AUD 3.2m outstanding** (DD-003; change-control 8.1, discharge 9.2). The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists.
- The Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion." This would leave the target encumbered, and leave us depending on the Seller's goodwill after we have paid.

**Pushback:** require a current **payout letter**, **direct repayment from Completion funds** in the funds flow, and **executed security releases** delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval, which we do not have. The debt must also flow through the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

### H. Employee bonuses: funds flow (DD-005)
The parenthetical "a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised" is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits. The Disclosure Letter (item 5) confirms the AUD 420,000 is absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. If the bonuses are triggered at Completion, the liability sits in the **Company**, which means we would bear it.

**Pushback:** either show the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a **specific funds-flow line item** deducted from the price (or treated as Debt/Transaction Costs), or have the Seller fund it directly. Back this with a specific indemnity for any shortfall or associated tax or super.

### I. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1, DD-004 / DD-010)
- DD-004 clause 7.3 makes the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. As the Seller itself concedes, that figure is not independently verified. We should not assume it is either paid or unpaid.
- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment, so ownership of the SOW3 IP is uncertain. An indemnity confined to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover title, infringement, injunction or re-development risk.

**Pushback:** broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted use of the Ironquay deliverables. Keep the SOW3 cure path: payment of any properly due amount plus a **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant. Request independent evidence of the payment status.

### J. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
The Seller says it is "not expected to be material." That conclusion is premature. The Disclosure Letter (item 6) states the investigation is preliminary and that access, scope and any notification duty are **unestablished**. Consistent with our playbook, we should **not** characterise this as a confirmed breach or put a dollar figure on it. We should equally reject the Seller's "not material" characterisation.

**Pushback:** add covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete a proper investigation (ideally forensic), give the Buyer regular updates and copies of findings, and obtain Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual notifications. The matter should also be addressed through a specific indemnity or warranty excluded from the general disclosure, so it cannot be "disclosed away."

### K. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
The Seller asserts that the three renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) are "ordinary course." The Disclosure Letter (item 8) concedes it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that the documents should be read together.

**Our position:** this needs **assessment**, not an automatic answer either way. Do not seek automatic Debt classification or a price deduction. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label either. Request the contracts, the timing and the termination rights. If the renewals turn out to be pre-Completion commitments outside the ordinary course, deal with them through working-capital or Debt definitions, or a specific warranty.

### L. Tax / IP
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are **not settled**: our playbook treats Tax and IP terms as **OPEN**. Reject the characterisation and keep Tax (a covenant/indemnity regime) and IP as separate categories. Note for internal planning that we are not assuming unlimited liability or any agreed resolution. These remain live negotiation points.

### M. Title evidence (DD-012)
The Seller relies solely on the share register in DD-012. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) itself says this is only the source relied on and does not represent Buyer verification. An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof.

**Pushback:** require independent evidence, including ASIC company extract and history, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, issue and transfer records, constitution and shareholder agreements (pre-emption rights), board and shareholder authorisations, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or encumbrances. Title must sit in the fundamental warranty regime (see B).

### N. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller's position on these is not in the Update, but the Disclosure Letter characterises them as notification-only (lease) and assignment-restriction-only (Mossvale). These are **the Seller's readings**. Counsel should confirm them against the full lease and Mossvale contract, checking change-of-control definitions in particular. Add warranties that no consent is required, and make lease notification a Completion deliverable.

---

## 3. Inconsistencies to put to the Seller

The Update and the Disclosure Letter contradict each other in places:

- **Bluefen:** "addressed" in the Update, but no consent and no conditions evidence per DL item 2.
- **Riverlark:** "addressed by a release," but not repaid and no discharge per DL item 3.
- **Bonuses:** "agreed price mechanics" in the funds flow, but DL item 5 concedes they are omitted.

These gaps support our pushback and should be raised expressly.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Must-haves (do not trade):**
1. **Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] framing and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"** in writing. Nothing is agreed.
2. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
3. **Separate fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Delete the "applies to all Claims" override.
4. **Bluefen:** condition precedent for effective consent plus evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone.
5. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed releases at Completion.
6. **Independent title evidence.** DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Core limitation package (revert to opening positions; no fallback authority held):**
7. Cap of **25% / AUD 6.0m**. Do not offer 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
8. De minimis **AUD 5,000**; basket **AUD 50,000, tipping**.
9. General claims period **24 months**. 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval.

**Disclosure and knowledge:**
10. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure and require specific fair disclosure. Update the disclosure date from 22 September 2026, with no cure by updated disclosure.
11. Delete the buyer-knowledge exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be Seller-side, with named persons and reasonable enquiry.

**Specific items:**
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs shown as a funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller, backed by an indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and use; keep the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment); verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
14. **DD-006:** covenants to preserve evidence, investigate and update us, plus a specific protection. Assume no confirmed breach, harm or amount, and reject the "not material" label.
15. **Sandbar:** request documents and assess. No automatic Debt treatment, and no acceptance of "ordinary course."
16. **Tax/IP:** record that both are **OPEN** and kept as separate categories.
17. **Lease/Mossvale:** verify the Seller's no-consent readings and add supporting warranties.

**Escalation note:** The Seller opened at our 20% cap fallback and our 18-month fallback. This suggests they may expect us to "meet in the middle" below our fallbacks. Amelia Frost should be told about this before any concession strategy is discussed. Until she gives written authority, the team should hold at our opening positions.

- There is no receipt of payment and no confirmatory assignment, so ownership of the SOW3 IP is uncertain. An indemnity confined to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover title, infringement, injunction or re-development risk.

**Pushback:** broaden the indemnity to cover all loss from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted use of the Ironquay deliverables. Keep the SOW3 cure path: payment of any properly due amount plus a **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable or pre-Completion covenant. Request independent evidence of the payment status.

### J. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
The Seller says it is "not expected to be material." That conclusion is premature. The Disclosure Letter (item 6) states the investigation is preliminary and that access, scope and any notification duty are **unestablished**. Consistent with our playbook, we should **not** characterise this as a confirmed breach or put a dollar figure on it. We should equally reject the Seller's "not material" characterisation.

**Pushback:** add covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete a proper investigation (ideally forensic), give the Buyer regular updates and copies of findings, and obtain Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual notifications. The matter should also be addressed through a specific indemnity or warranty excluded from the general disclosure, so it cannot be "disclosed away."

### K. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
The Seller asserts that the three renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) are "ordinary course." The Disclosure Letter (item 8) concedes it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that the documents should be read together.

**Our position:** this needs **assessment**, not an automatic answer either way. Do not seek automatic Debt classification or a price deduction. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label either. Request the contracts, the timing and the termination rights. If the renewals turn out to be pre-Completion commitments outside the ordinary course, deal with them through working-capital or Debt definitions, or a specific warranty.

### L. Tax / IP
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are **not settled**: our playbook treats Tax and IP terms as **OPEN**. Reject the characterisation and keep Tax (a covenant/indemnity regime) and IP as separate categories. Note for internal planning that we are not assuming unlimited liability or any agreed resolution. These remain live negotiation points.

### M. Title evidence (DD-012)
The Seller relies solely on the share register in DD-012. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) itself says this is only the source relied on and does not represent Buyer verification. An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof.

**Pushback:** require independent evidence, including ASIC company extract and history, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, issue and transfer records, constitution and shareholder agreements (pre-emption rights), board and shareholder authorisations, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or encumbrances. Title must sit in the fundamental warranty regime (see B).

### N. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller's position on these is not in the Update, but the Disclosure Letter characterises them as notification-only (lease) and assignment-restriction-only (Mossvale). These are **the Seller's readings**. Counsel should confirm them against the full lease and Mossvale contract, checking change-of-control definitions in particular. Add warranties that no consent is required, and make lease notification a Completion deliverable.
